method: Scoped web search and selected primary-source sections; not an exhaustive market survey. Dates describe retrieval/review, not necessarily publication. Gap statements are Simurgh analysis.

sources.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents — Anthropic
sources.text: Distinguishes transcripts from actual final environment state. Recommends inspecting failed transcripts, balanced tasks, repeated trials and checking grader validity. Simurgh implication: expose source outcomes and failures with denominators; do not equate completion claims with receiver effects.

sources.title: Evaluate agent workflows — OpenAI documentation
sources.text: Trace grading covers model calls, tools, guardrails and handoffs; datasets and evaluation runs support repeated comparison. Simurgh implication: a trace dashboard is established functionality, not evidence of novelty. Our scope connects outcomes to authorization and observed effects.

sources.title: Misalignment monitoring — OpenAI documentation
sources.text: A flag requires investigation; it does not establish wrongdoing. Coverage and automatic stopping depend on API/context. Blocked workflows must not automatically retry. Prior actions may already have completed; registering a block does not establish execution stopped. Simurgh implication: keep alerts, dispatch, acknowledgments and receiver effects distinct; actual provider integration remains unvalidated.

sources.title: Security best practices — Model Context Protocol, 2026-07-28
sources.text: MCP guidance forbids token passthrough and explains audience-validation, confused-deputy and audit-trail risks. Simurgh implication: synthetic credentials do not prove interoperable real MCP/OAuth lifecycle behavior; owned-service validation is still needed.

sources.title: Measurements for understanding the pace of AI development inside frontier labs — Anthropic
sources.text: Proposes monitoring coverage, review latency and escalation rate as reportable measures, and calls for third-party testing. Simurgh implication: bounded concurrent fixtures do not establish sustained deployment coverage, human review latency or independent observation.

gaps.title: Independent evidence custody
gaps.evidence: Source-bound archives and local replay are available; the owner will arrange a classmate.
gaps.remaining: Author-operated records cannot prove honest-host completeness or outside observation.
gaps.next: Classmate checks pinned archives independently and returns their own receipt and discrepancies.

gaps.title: Live provider alerts and identity lifecycle
gaps.evidence: Local signed alerts, stop/revoke ordering and authenticated owned-receiver fixtures exist.
gaps.remaining: No entitled provider project has demonstrated real alert delivery, active-session revocation or OAuth/MCP interoperability.
gaps.next: Use an owned project with alert-read/webhook and identity permissions; record benign lifecycle tests without inducing abuse.

gaps.title: Harder tasks across model families
gaps.evidence: Phase 10 retains 48 generations and 144 matched branches from one model setting.
gaps.remaining: Short author-held tasks do not demonstrate transfer to independently held multi-turn tasks or other models.
gaps.next: Preregister externally held tasks, matched baselines and a fixed model/spend budget before fresh inference.

gaps.title: Sustained operation and timing
gaps.evidence: Phase 13 covers 60 bounded concurrent/restart fixtures and 210 final calls.
gaps.remaining: Logical-clock fixtures do not establish wall-clock monitor expiry, live queues, review latency or interruption of admitted work.
gaps.next: Define a representative owned deployment and load/coverage/latency objectives, then retain failed and unknown outcomes.

gaps.title: Real-data evidence privacy
gaps.evidence: Phase 14 projects all 144 outcomes with explicit omissions and synthetic canary checks.
gaps.remaining: This is not an access-control, retention/deletion or anonymity proof for real traces.
gaps.next: Specify data owners and retention rules; independently review whether omissions conceal material failures.

gaps.title: Browser and native macOS measurements
gaps.evidence: Portable discovery and explicit managed-policy detection implemented; Node/Python parity passes.
gaps.remaining: Managed Chromium blocks local pages; Linux cannot establish macOS/CryptoKit outcomes.
gaps.next: Run fresh browser receipts and native checks on permitted matching machines.

gaps.title: Legacy gate maintenance
gaps.evidence: Phase 16 migrated retired HTTP 410 assertions and maintained exact reproduce inventory beside frozen pin.
gaps.remaining: Historical artifacts retain original results. Current aggregate validation is recorded separately.
gaps.next: Use the maintained inventory and preserve frozen evidence on future migrations.

gaps.title: Phase 8 local review
gaps.evidence: Full local source/test review completed; 24 tests and a separate 46-row/92-snapshot replay passed.
gaps.remaining: Same-workspace manual review under the trusted-host model, not external certification.
gaps.next: Include review scope and trust assumptions in classmate handoff.
